2.2.1.2-r1.burton_quote: the more they eat the more they nourish themselves: eat and live, as the proverb is, not knowing that only repairs man which is well concocted, not that which is devoured

2.2.1.2-r2.burton_quote: Melancholy men most part have good appetites, but ill digestion

2.2.1.2-r3.burton_quote: than which (saith Avicenna) nothing is worse, to feed on diversity of meats, or overmuch, Sertorius-like in lucem coenare, and as commonly they do in Muscovy and Iceland, to prolong their meals all day long, or all night

2.2.1.2-r4.burton_quote: to choose one of many, and to feed on that alone

2.2.1.2-r5.burton_quote: he would have his highness to dine or sup alone, without all his honourable attendance & courtly company, with a private friend or so, a dish or two, a cup of Rhenish wine

2.2.1.2-r7.burton_quote: Alexander Severus loved Hares and Apples above all other meats
2.2.1.2-r7.translation: he had a hare every day
